take_homes: Default to one agent. Splitting has to pass the test 'could one prompt do this?' and needs a reason: access, dialect or stance.
Information gets lost at handoffs between agents. A human gate or a propose-then-approve step is the control, and it is the thing to check.
The audit checks the handoffs and not whether the answer is true. Someone still has to verify the output.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with one agent, and ask IT what the tool can reach and what it costs per month for 40 people.
monday.stop_condition: No cost or time comparison against the current manual process, or IT has not approved it for finance data.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: The 'one agent unless proven otherwise' and 'worst thing it could do with that access' framing treats this as a capability the organisation designs and governs, not a licence. I still don't have a number, so I'm not convinced.

one_line: The split-or-don't rule is useful and honest about the risks, but the exercises run four sessions for half an hour with no cost or payback figure, and I'm told to accept an answer I can't check.
